tests.mutation: Applicability.Of excluded the date itself (`saleOrExchangeDate > ApplicableFrom` for `saleOrExchangeDate >= ApplicableFrom`), so a sale on 24 December 2002 was outside the section; this test went red. It went red too with Applicability.ApplicableFrom set to the corpus's pinned baseline date (`new(2026, 1, 1)` for `new(2002, 12, 24)`), with it set a day early (`new(2002, 12, 23)`), and with SectionApplicability.Authority citing exclusion-of-gain's `§ 1.121-1(a)` (`MapEntries.ExclusionOfGain.Locator` for `MapEntries.EffectiveDate.Locator`). Citing retroactive-election's locator did NOT turn it red: both entries cite `§ 1.121-1(f)`, so the locator cannot tell them apart.

Applicability.Of found every sale within the section (`true` for `saleOrExchangeDate >= ApplicableFrom`); this test went red. It went red too with Applicability.ApplicableFrom a day early (`new(2002, 12, 23)` for `new(2002, 12, 24)`), with the finding recording the rule's date instead of the caller's (`new SectionApplicability(ApplicableFrom, ...` for `new SectionApplicability(saleOrExchangeDate, ...`), and with Authority citing exclusion-of-gain's `§ 1.121-1(a)`.

Handlers.EffectiveDate defaulted a missing date to the effective date (`request.SaleOrExchangeDate ?? Applicability.ApplicableFrom` for `Demand(request.SaleOrExchangeDate, ...)`), so a request with no date resolved as within the section; this test went red. It went red too with a missing date answered as an unresolved `MissingRulesData` decline citing `§ 1.121-1(f)` instead of refused.

Handlers.EffectiveDate defaulted a missing date to the effective date (`request.SaleOrExchangeDate ?? Applicability.ApplicableFrom` for `Demand(request.SaleOrExchangeDate, ...)`), so `Registry.Resolve("effective-date", RuleRequest.Empty)` resolved as within the section; this test went red. It went red too with a missing date answered as an unresolved `MissingRulesData` decline instead of refused.

Applicability.Gate let every sale proceed (`finding => true` for `finding => finding.Applies`); this test went red. It went red too with the decline's reason `MissingRulesData`, and `RequiresInterpretation`, for `OutsideCurrentScope`; with it citing the gated entry's own locator (`entry.Locator` for `finding.Authority`, § 1.121-1(a)); with the retroactive election dropped from the message; with `see § 1.121-4(j)` dropped from it; and with the gated entry's id dropped from it. Citing retroactive-election's locator (`MapEntries.RetroactiveElection.Locator` for `finding.Authority`) did NOT turn it red: both entries cite `§ 1.121-1(f)`, so the locator cannot tell them apart, and the message is what names the election.

Applicability.Gate declined every sale (`finding => false` for `finding => finding.Applies`); this test went red. It went red too with Applicability.Of excluding the date itself (`saleOrExchangeDate > ApplicableFrom` for `saleOrExchangeDate >= ApplicableFrom`), and with the gate evaluating the day before the effective date instead of the caller's date (`Of(ApplicableFrom.AddDays(-1))` for `Of(date)`).

Applicability.Of found only the effective date itself within the section (`saleOrExchangeDate == ApplicableFrom` for `saleOrExchangeDate >= ApplicableFrom`); this test went red and every other gate and effective-date test stayed green. It went red too with Applicability.Gate declining every sale (`finding => false`), and with the gate evaluating the day before the effective date instead of the caller's date.

Applicability.Gate defaulted a missing date to the effective date (`saleOrExchangeDate ?? ApplicableFrom` for `?? throw new ArgumentException(...)`), so a missing date proceeded; this test went red. It went red too with the refusal's ParamName `"saleOrExchangeDate"` for `nameof(Requests.EffectiveDateRequest.SaleOrExchangeDate)`, and with the gated entry's id dropped from its message.

Citing residence-cooperative-apartment's locator (`MapEntries.ResidenceCooperativeApartment.Locator`) did NOT turn it red: both entries cite `§ 1.121-1(b)`, so the locator cannot tell them apart.
